claim: Conformal prediction converts almost any predictive algorithm into prediction intervals or sets with finite-sample marginal coverage under exchangeability.
quote: Conformal prediction (CP) converts almost any predictive algorithm into prediction intervals or sets with finite-sample marginal coverage under exchangeability [1][2][3].

claim: Deployment data, however, are rarely exchangeable with development data.
quote: Deployment data, however, are rarely exchangeable with development data.

claim: Geographic transfer, changing case mix, sensor replacement, policy changes, and temporal drift can alter the covariate distribution P X , the conditional outcome law P Y |X , or both.
quote: Geographic transfer, changing case mix, sensor replacement, policy changes, and temporal drift can alter the covariate distribution P X , the conditional outcome law P Y |X , or both

claim: One source describes the difficulty for covariate shift directly: exchangeability of calibration and test points fails, which makes the standard coverage argument void.
quote: The fundamental challenge for conformal prediction is that exchangeability of calibration and test points fails, making the standard coverage argument void.

claim: Weighted conformal prediction extends validity to covariate shift by weighting calibration scores with the density ratio.
quote: Weighted conformal prediction (WCP) extends validity to covariate shift by weighting calibration scores with the density ratio w(x) = dQ X (x)/dP X (x) [5].

claim: A review of Tibshirani et al. describes the method as designed for covariate shift where the likelihood ratio between training and test covariate distributions is known.
quote: Specifically, they propose weighted conformal prediction (WCP) to deal with covariate shifts where the likelihood ratio between the training P X and test PX covariate distributions is known.

claim: Gibbs and Candès describe Tibshirani et al.'s reweighting approach as requiring the conditional distribution of Y|X to be constant between training and testing and the likelihood ratio to be either known or very accurately estimated.
quote: [33] showed that valid prediction sets can be obtained by re-weighting the calibration data using the likelihood ratio between P 1 and P 0 . However, this requires the conditional distribution of Y |X to be constant between training and testing and the likelihood ratio P 1 (X)/P 0 (X) to be either known or very accurately estimated.

claim: A further source states that when likelihood ratios must be estimated, coverage degrades at a rate controlled by the estimation error.
quote: When likelihood ratios must be estimated, coverage degrades at a rate controlled by the estimation error (Barber et al., 2023).

claim: Adaptive conformal inference is presented as achieving the desired coverage frequency over long-time intervals irrespective of the true data generating process.
quote: our adaptive approach provably achieves the desired coverage frequency over long-time intervals irrespective of the true data generating process.

claim: The same paper describes Cauchois et al. as developing prediction sets valid whenever the two distributions are close in f-divergence.
quote: On the other hand, Cauchois et al. [10] develop methods for forming prediction sets that are valid whenever P 1 and P 0 are close in f -divergence.

claim: One source reports that, for estimated weighted conformal prediction, the bound inherits an approximation term and is not relabeled exact.
quote: oracle test-point WCP has its stated finite-sample guarantee; estimated WCP inherits an approximation term and is not relabeled "exact."
locator: sec. Setting and conformal baselines, para 9

claim: Another lists simultaneous covariate and label shift, with partially identifiable likelihood ratios, as an open challenge.
quote: Extending the framework to simultaneous covariate and label shift with partially identifiable likelihood ratios is an open challenge.

claim: The original work states that a weighted version of conformal prediction yields distribution-free prediction intervals when the likelihood ratio between test and training covariate distributions is known, or can be estimated accurately with a large set of unlabeled test covariates.
quote: we show that a weighted version of conformal prediction can be used to compute distribution-free prediction intervals for problems in which the test and training covariate distributions differ, but the likelihood ratio between these two distributions is known---or, in practice, can be estimated accurately with access to a large set of unlabeled data (test covariate points).

claim: A later tabular-regression paper restates the known-ratio result as marginal coverage of at least 1 - alpha under covariate shift, provided the likelihood ratios are exactly known.
quote: The weighted quantile of this distribution yields a prediction set with marginal coverage guarantee P^{test} (Y_{n+1} in C_w(X_{n+1})) >= 1 -alpha, even under covariate shift, provided the likelihood ratios are exactly known.

claim: The same paper says that when ratios must be estimated, coverage degrades at a rate controlled by the estimation error.
quote: When likelihood ratios must be estimated, coverage degrades at a rate controlled by the estimation error (Barber et al., 2023).

claim: The adaptive conformal inference paper adds that reweighting requires Y|X to be constant between training and testing and the ratio to be known or very accurately estimated.
quote: [33] showed that valid prediction sets can be obtained by re-weighting the calibration data using the likelihood ratio between P 1 and P 0 . However, this requires the conditional distribution of Y |X to be constant between training and testing and the likelihood ratio P 1 (X)/P 0 (X) to be either known or very accurately estimated.

claim: The DriftGuard audit paper says that with estimated ratios, finite-sample validity generally needs additional conditions or doubly robust constructions.
quote: When ratios are estimated, finitesample validity generally needs additional conditions or doubly robust constructions [11]; our estimated-weight results are therefore empirical rather than advertised as exact guarantees.
locator: sec. Setting and conformal baselines, para 6

claim: The DriftGuard paper (R3) separates oracle from estimated weighting: it states that oracle test-point weighted conformal prediction has its stated finite-sample guarantee, while estimated weighted conformal prediction inherits an approximation term and is not relabeled "exact."
quote: oracle test-point WCP has its stated finite-sample guarantee; estimated WCP inherits an approximation term and is not relabeled "exact."
locator: sec. Setting and conformal baselines, para 9

claim: A weight-clipping study reports that weighted conformal prediction can suffer significant undercoverage when the density ratio is unbounded or must be learned.
quote: While weighted conformal prediction (WCP) is designed to handle such shifts, it can suffer from significant undercoverage when the density ratio between the distributions is unbounded and/or must be learned.

claim: A training-conditional analysis reports that its treatment extends to estimated likelihood ratios.
quote: The analysis extends to estimated likelihood ratios and to tail functionals estimated from an unlabeled source sample, which yields a fully finite-sample certificate.

claim: The tabular-regression paper lists simultaneous covariate and label shift, with partially identifiable ratios, as an open challenge.
quote: Extending the framework to simultaneous covariate and label shift with partially identifiable likelihood ratios is an open challenge.

claim: The label-shift classification study examines reweighting of conformal and calibration procedures whenever some unlabeled data from the target distribution is available.
quote: we examine the right way to achieve UQ by reweighting the aforementioned conformal and calibration procedures whenever some unlabeled data from the target distribution is available.

claim: The Bayesian-score paper reports that, under stronger shift, all methods incur some coverage loss due to pseudo-label-based density-ratio estimation.
quote: Under stronger shift, all methods incur some coverage loss due to pseudo-label-based density-ratio estimation.

claim: The conformal Bayes study states that its two approaches restore nominal target-domain coverage through importance-weighted conformal calibration.
quote: identifying two complementary approaches that restore nominal target-domain coverage through importance-weighted conformal calibration but operate through independent mechanisms.

claim: Barber and coauthors state that conformal prediction's validity relies on exchangeability of the data and symmetry of the model fitting algorithm.
quote: Conformal prediction is a popular, modern technique for providing valid predictive inference for arbitrary machine learning models. Its validity relies on the assumptions of exchangeability of the data, and symmetry of the given model fitting algorithm as a function of the data.

claim: The paper introduces weighted quantiles to provide robustness against distribution drift.
quote: we employ weighted quantiles to introduce robustness against distribution drift, and design a new randomization technique to allow for algorithms that do not treat data points symmetrically.

claim: The authors claim substantially less loss of coverage under drift, while matching existing coverage guarantees when the data are exchangeable.
quote: Our new methods are provably robust, with substantially less loss of coverage when exchangeability is violated due to distribution drift or other challenging features of real data, while also achieving the same coverage guarantees as existing conformal prediction methods if the data points are in fact exchangeable.

claim: A covariate-shift paper that cites this work states that weighted conformal prediction gives marginal coverage of at least 1 - alpha when the likelihood ratios are exactly known.
quote: The weighted quantile of this distribution yields a prediction set with marginal coverage guarantee P^{test} (Y_{n+1} in C_w(X_{n+1})) >= 1 -alpha, even under covariate shift, provided the likelihood ratios are exactly known.

claim: The same paper says coverage degrades at a rate controlled by the estimation error when the ratios must be estimated, and attributes this to Barber et al.
quote: When likelihood ratios must be estimated, coverage degrades at a rate controlled by the estimation error (Barber et al., 2023).

claim: The auditing paper takes a similar position, saying that estimated weighted conformal prediction inherits an approximation term and is not relabeled exact.
quote: oracle test-point WCP has its stated finite-sample guarantee; estimated WCP inherits an approximation term and is not relabeled "exact."
locator: sec. Setting and conformal baselines, para 9

claim: The Wasserstein paper notes that prior studies bound the coverage gap with total variation distance, which it says cannot identify how the gap changes under distribution shift at a given alpha.
quote: Prior studies bound the gap using total variation distance, which cannot identify the gap changes under distribution shift at a given $α$.

claim: Gibbs and Candès state that, while previous conformal inference methods rely on the assumption that the data points are exchangeable, their adaptive approach provably achieves the desired coverage frequency over long-time intervals irrespective of the true data generating process.
quote: While previous conformal inference methods rely on the assumption that the data points are exchangeable, our adaptive approach provably achieves the desired coverage frequency over long-time intervals irrespective of the true data generating process.

claim: The ACI authors describe their Proposition 4.1 as an agnostic guarantee of correct long-term empirical coverage frequency and as an approximately tight bound on worst-case behaviour right after initialization.
quote: So, we view Proposition 4.1 as both an agnostic guarantee that shows that our method gives the correct long-term empirical coverage frequency irrespective of the true data generating process, and as an approximately tight bound on the worst-case behaviour immediately after initialization.
locator: sec. Coverage guarantees 4.1 Distribution-free results, para 51

claim: The same paper says that, when the distribution shift is small and the prediction algorithm takes a certain simple form, ACI additionally obtains approximate marginal coverage at most time steps.
quote: Moreover, when the distribution shift is small and the prediction algorithm takes a certain simple form we show that ACI will additionally obtain approximate marginal coverage at most time steps.

claim: The abstract of the follow-up work by Gibbs and Candès states that ACI requires knowledge of the rate of change of the data-generating mechanism.
quote: unlike ACI, which requires knowledge of the rate of change of the data-generating mechanism

claim: Error-quantified Conformal Inference establishes a long-term coverage guarantee under arbitrary dependence and distribution shift.
quote: We establish a long-term coverage guarantee for ECI under arbitrary dependence and distribution shift.

claim: A dropout-informed variant reports that its long-run coverage guarantee is score-agnostic, inherited from ACI itself rather than a new property of studentization.
quote: the resulting long-run coverage guarantee is scoreagnostic-inherited from ACI itself rather than a new property of studentization (Lemma 1)

claim: Another study notes that ACI only adapts the quantile threshold and cannot shift the interval center.
quote: However, ACI only adapts the quantile threshold -- it cannot shift the interval center.

claim: The robust validation work presents a method whose prediction sets give almost exactly the right coverage level for any test distribution in an f-divergence ball around the training population.
quote: We present a method that produces prediction sets (almost exactly) giving the right coverage level for any test distribution in an f-divergence ball around the training population.

claim: Robust validation achieves nearly valid coverage in finite samples, under only the condition that the training data be exchangeable.
quote: The method, based on conformal inference, achieves (nearly) valid coverage in finite samples, under only the condition that the training data be exchangeable.

claim: Robust validation also estimates the amount of expected future shift, and its authors prove consistency of the estimators.
quote: An essential component of our methodology is to estimate the amount of expected future data shift and build robustness to it; we develop estimators and prove their consistency for protection and validity of uncertainty estimates under shifts.

claim: The fine-grained framework splits the problem differently, reweighting training samples for an identifiable covariate shift while protecting against worst-case conditional shift bounded in an f-divergence ball.
quote: We propose to reweight the training samples to adjust for an identifiable covariate shift while protecting against worst-case conditional distribution shift bounded in an $f$-divergence ball.

claim: Adaptive conformal inference is described by its authors as an agnostic guarantee of correct long-term empirical coverage frequency irrespective of the true data generating process.
quote: So, we view Proposition 4.1 as both an agnostic guarantee that shows that our method gives the correct long-term empirical coverage frequency irrespective of the true data generating process, and as an approximately tight bound on the worst-case behaviour immediately after initialization.
locator: sec. Coverage guarantees 4.1 Distribution-free results, para 51

claim: Gibbs and Candès describe the f-divergence method of Cauchois et al. as forming prediction sets that are valid whenever P 1 and P 0 are close in f -divergence.
quote: Cauchois et al. [10] develop methods for forming prediction sets that are valid whenever P 1 and P 0 are close in f -divergence.

claim: A robust conformal runtime-verification study assumes a known upper bound on the f-divergence between deployment and design distributions.
quote: To address these challenges, we assume to know an upper bound on the statistical distance (in terms of an f-divergence) between the distributions at deployment and design time, and we utilize techniques based on robust conformal prediction.

claim: One audit paper states that when density ratios are estimated, finite-sample validity generally needs additional conditions or doubly robust constructions.
quote: When ratios are estimated, finitesample validity generally needs additional conditions or doubly robust constructions [11]; our estimated-weight results are therefore empirical rather than advertised as exact guarantees.
locator: sec. Setting and conformal baselines, para 6

claim: A study of training-conditional coverage reports that its analysis extends to estimated likelihood ratios.
quote: The analysis extends to estimated likelihood ratios and to tail functionals estimated from an unlabeled source sample, which yields a fully finite-sample certificate.

claim: A tabular-regression paper reports adaptive prediction sets that achieve near-optimal conditional coverage rates whenever the likelihood ratio is estimable at a sufficient rate.
quote: paired with adaptive prediction sets (APS) that achieve near-optimal conditional coverage rates whenever the likelihood ratio is estimable at a sufficient rate (Theorem 4.3).

claim: A label-shift Bayesian score paper reports coverage loss under stronger shift because density ratios are estimated from pseudo-labels.
quote: Under stronger shift, all methods incur some coverage loss due to pseudo-label-based density-ratio estimation.

claim: A tabular-regression paper on covariate shift lists extending the framework to simultaneous covariate and label shift with partially identifiable likelihood ratios as an open challenge.
quote: Extending the framework to simultaneous covariate and label shift with partially identifiable likelihood ratios is an open challenge.

claim: The audit paper establishes a sharp [0,1] identified set for target coverage under unrestricted conditional shift.
quote: We establish exact and approximate detectability bounds, a minimax testing consequence, and a sharp $[0,1]$ identified set for target coverage under unrestricted conditional shift.

claim: A fine-grained robust method handles an identifiable covariate shift while protecting against worst-case conditional shift bounded in an f-divergence ball.
quote: We propose to reweight the training samples to adjust for an identifiable covariate shift while protecting against worst-case conditional distribution shift bounded in an $f$-divergence ball.
